plan: [Compute posterior of common value given my signal 17. Since noise is uniform and for C in 20–29 s−C lies in [-20,20], likelihood is equal, so posterior is uniform on 20–29. Thus E[C|S=17]=(20+29)/2=24.5. In symmetric equilibrium bid E[C|S], so bid 24.5 to maximize expected profit.]

[Compute posterior over the common value given my signal 41: common ∈ [21,29], prior uniform. The probability I beat a given opponent at common c is ((61-c)/40), so winning probability ∝ ((61-c)/40)^2. Conditioning on winning gives E[common | win, s=41] ≈ 24.7. In a second-price common-value auction, bid this conditional expectation to avoid the winner's curse and maximize long-run profit.]

[Given my signal 33 and noise in [-20,20], the signal doesn't change the uniform prior on the common value (20–29). Posterior mean = 24.5. To avoid the winner's curse in this common-value, second-price auction, bid the posterior expected common value. This maximizes my expected profit net of paying the second-highest bid.]
